newsitem.title: USA: Playboy to appeal part of Telecom Act.
newsitem.headline: Playboy to appeal part of Telecom Act.

text.p: Playboy Entertainment Group said it will challenge a U.S. District Court ruling that requires cable television operators to scramble audio and video portions of sexually explicit programming.

Playboy, the operator of the Playboy TV cable television channel, said in a statement that it had requested the court to block enforcement of a provision of the Telecommunications Act of 1996 that would require the scrambled television signal.
Playboy contends that available technology makes this provision of the Telecommunications Act unnecessary.
Playboy said Section 505 of the law requires new blocking equipment be installed in millions of cable homes, regardless of whether a customer needs or wants it.

If the blocking equipment is not provided, cable systems are limited to offering Playboy programming between 2200 in the evening and 0600 in the morning, putting the pay television service under the same limits as free, broadcast television, Playboy said.
Under the law, other premium and pay-per-view channels would not be blocked, even when they show the same programming, Playboy said.
